title: Sherry
subtitle: Flor, solera and Palomino
objectives: Describe where Sherry is made and from what

steps.title: Jerez and Palomino
steps.body: Sherry comes from the area around Jerez de la Frontera, Sanlúcar de Barrameda and El Puerto de Santa María, in Andalusia. The main grape is Palomino, which makes a neutral, low-acid base wine. The chalky white soil, called albariza, holds water through hot, dry summers. Sweet styles use Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel.

steps.title: Flor and the solera
steps.body: After fermentation the wine is fortified. Wines for Fino are taken to about 15%; at this level a layer of yeast called flor grows on the surface, protecting the wine from oxygen and adding notes of bread, almonds and salt. Wines for Oloroso go to 17%, which stops flor, so they age with oxygen. Most Sherry ages in a solera, a system of barrels where young wine tops up older wine.

steps.prompt: What does flor do to a Fino Sherry?
options: Protects it from oxygen and adds bready, salty notes
steps.explanation: Flor is a layer of yeast that shields the wine from air and adds its own distinctive flavours.

steps.title: How a solera works
steps.body: A solera is a set of barrels in tiers. Wine for bottling is drawn from the oldest tier, called the solera, but never more than about a third at a time. That tier is topped up from the next oldest, called the first criadera, and so on, with new wine entering at the youngest tier. The blend keeps a steady style and gains average age.
steps.highlight: Old tier drawn, refilled from younger

steps.prompt: Put the solera's movements in order, starting with bottling.
items: Draw wine from the oldest tier
Refill it from the first criadera
Refill that from the second criadera
Add new wine to the youngest tier
steps.explanation: Each tier passes some of its wine to the older one, so the style stays consistent year after year.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sherry is made from Palomino on the albariza soils of Jerez
Flor protects Fino from air; Oloroso ages without it
The solera blends wines of many ages for consistency
